rungs.stem: In a parable Jesus tells in Matthew 25, a rich man is about to leave on a long journey. He calls three of his servants, hands each of them some of his money to look after while he is gone, and departs. How much does he give the first servant, the second, and the third?
choices: Five talents, then two talents, then one talent
Three talents, then three talents, then three talents
Ten talents, then five talents, then one talent
Two talents, then two talents, then two talents
rungs.answer: Five talents, then two talents, then one talent
rungs.context: Matthew 25:15 KJV: 'And unto one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one; to every man according to his several ability; and straightway took his journey.' Source: KJV Matthew 25.

rungs.stem: The 'talent' the master hands out in Matthew 25 is not a small coin. In the ancient world a talent was a unit of WEIGHT -- specifically, of silver or gold. Roughly how heavy was one talent of silver?
choices: About seventy-five pounds
About one ounce
About one pound
About four hundred pounds
rungs.context: A biblical talent weighed roughly 70-90 pounds. One talent of silver was worth about 6,000 denarii -- roughly twenty years of a common labourer's wages -- so even the servant given only one talent was handed a small fortune, and the servant given five was made responsible for an enormous sum. Source: learnreligions.com/what-is-a-talent-700699 ; pastorjasonelder.com/bible-facts-all/how-much-did-a-talent-weigh.

rungs.stem: In the parable, the first two servants take the money the master has left them and trade with it -- doubling what they were given. The third servant, afraid of the master, does something very different with his share.
choices: He digs a hole in the ground and buries it
He lends it out to moneychangers for interest
He gives it away to beggars in the marketplace
He hides it inside a hollow beam in the roof
rungs.answer: He digs a hole in the ground and buries it
rungs.context: Matthew 25:18 KJV: 'But he that had received one went and digged in the earth, and hid his lord's money.' Later in the same parable the master rebukes him precisely because he did not even lend it to the exchangers to earn interest (Matthew 25:27). Source: KJV Matthew 25.

rungs.stem: The master finally comes home and settles accounts. To EACH of the two servants who doubled their money he uses the same congratulatory line, word for word. Which line does he say?
choices: 'Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things'
'Blessed art thou among my servants; thy portion shall be tenfold what thou hadst before'
'Because thou hast been diligent, thou shalt sit at my right hand at the feast'
'Thou hast been wise beyond thy years; I shall give thee half of all my substance'
rungs.answer: 'Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things'
rungs.context: Matthew 25:21 KJV (and repeated word-for-word to the second servant at 25:23): 'Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.' Source: KJV Matthew 25.

rungs.stem: The scolded servant confesses he buried the money because he was afraid of his master. What does the master order done with the one buried talent he took back?
choices: Given to the servant who now has ten talents
Thrown into the fire so no one could use it
Divided equally between the two other servants
Kept in the master's own strongbox from then on
rungs.answer: Given to the servant who now has ten talents
rungs.context: Matthew 25:28 KJV: 'Take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which hath ten talents.' The line that follows -- 'unto every one that hath shall be given, and he shall have abundance' -- has been quoted for two thousand years as the Matthew Effect. Source: KJV Matthew 25.

rungs.stem: Right before the talents parable, Jesus tells another parable in Matthew 25 comparing the kingdom of heaven to ten young women who go out at night with their lamps to meet a bridegroom. Five of them are called wise; the other five are called something specific.
choices: Foolish
Idle
Faithless
Vain
rungs.context: Matthew 25:2 KJV: 'And five of them were wise, and five were foolish.' The wise five brought extra oil in vessels alongside their lamps; the foolish five brought only what was already in the wick. Source: KJV Matthew 25.

rungs.stem: The wedding party in Matthew 25 is delayed, and all ten of the women fall asleep waiting. Then a shout goes up and startles them all awake. At what hour of the night does the shout come, according to Matthew 25:6?
choices: At midnight
At the first watch, just after sundown
At cockcrow, near the third watch
At dawn, as the sky was reddening
rungs.context: Matthew 25:6 KJV: 'And at midnight there was a cry made, Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him.' The midnight timing is why the wise women's SPARE oil matters -- the ordinary wick oil has burned all evening and is running low just as the bridegroom finally arrives. Source: KJV Matthew 25.

rungs.stem: In the Ten Virgins parable, the foolish five run out to buy oil for their dying lamps and while they are gone the bridegroom arrives. The door is shut. When they finally get back and pound on it, crying 'Lord, Lord, open to us,' what four-word answer comes back from inside?
choices: 'I know you not'
'Depart from me, workers of iniquity'
'You have chosen darkness'
'The hour is spent'
rungs.context: Matthew 25:12 KJV: 'But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.' It is the parable's punchline -- the door already shut, the answer as flat as the shut door itself. Bonus: the English word 'talent' meaning a natural ability came out of the OTHER parable in this same chapter -- Old English 'talent' meant only a weight of silver; the sense of a gift entrusted for use developed by the mid-1400s from medieval preaching on Matthew 25. Source: KJV Matthew 25 ; etymonline.com/word/talent.
